subject: Combine more than two gl objects

messages.author: a59df4914e45df44
messages.subject: Combine more than two gl objects
parts:
Greetings,

I have a single SNP dataset that is now large enough (1,100 x 120k) that DArT supplied it in three files (gla, glb, glc), due to file size limitations. In order to analyze the data, I must use gl.join() or similar function. It appears that gl.join() will only accept two input files. My initial solution was recursive gl.join().

gl1 <- gl.join(gla,glb)
#this works fine

gl <- gl.join(gl1, glc)
>Starting gl.join
> Processing SNP data in genlight object 1
>  Processing SNP data in genlight object 2
>  Concatenating two genlight objects
>Error in rbind(deparse.level, ...) :
>  numbers of columns of arguments do not match

I don't understand how/why gl.join() changes the number of columns in the data. Is anyone familiar with a workaround? In the past I have used R to deconstruct and reconstruct the .csv files, and I will do this again if needed. I am hoping there is another way.

Thank you,
Mike

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Combine more than two gl objects
parts:
Hi Mike,

Maybe you are using an older version of dartR. To install the latest version, in which this problem has been solved, you can try the following:

# library required to install from github
library(devtools)
# installing beta version of dartR
install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@beta",build_manual = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)

# if you are working with R-studio restart your session with menu Session -> Restart R

library(dartR)

gl.data.new <- gl.join(gla, glb)
gl.data.new <- gl.join(gl.data.new, glc)

Please let us know whether this worked for you.

Cheers,
Luis

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: Combine more than two gl objects
parts:
Hi Mike,

The problem is that your DArT report has 17 duplicated SNPs. We are in talks with DArT to investigate the source of this issue.
In the meantime, I have modified the function gl.read.dart to check for duplicated SNPs. For the moment, the approach is to remove all the duplicated SNPs until we find the source of the issue.

Also, the names of the individuals in your metadata file should be unique and preferably in the same order as in DArT's report. I have modified this file for your convenience (attached).

You can use this updated version of gl.read.dart by installing the developing version of dartR by typing in the R console:

> library(devtools)
> install_github("green-striped-gecko/dartR@dev",build_manual = TRUE, build_vignettes = TRUE)

Cheers,
Luis
